docs.purpose: The last line of defence when part of the app crashes. Instead of a white screen, the user sees a short 'something went wrong' message, the underlying error text, and a Try Again button that attempts to re-render. It wraps both the whole app and, separately, the signed-in tab area.
docs.data_story: This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device. It holds no client-side store, so there is no local copy of server state to keep in sync. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`.

contracts: mobile/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:1-76 — no contract; it catches render errors

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: It is mounted twice — around the whole app and around the tab tree — so a change to its contract changes the crash behaviour of every surface at once.

inputs.why: Children only. Its real input is a thrown render error, which React hands it through getDerivedStateFromError.

outputs.why: It writes nothing; its handleReset clears local error state and re-renders the children.

state.why: A class component holding { hasError, errorMessage } — no store, no cache, no persistence.

session.why: It wraps the entire tree including the unauthenticated auth group, so it must render with no session.

disclosure.why: The caught error MESSAGE is rendered on screen to an unauthenticated principal; the component deliberately drops the full error object and componentStack, both of which can carry addresses and permit numbers.

checks.why: componentDidCatch logs the message only — never the error object or componentStack — because both can carry user PII (addresses, permit numbers, response bodies) into Sentry.

dumpDiagnostics() returns '' in production, so the second console.error is guarded — without the guard every production crash would emit a blank line to Sentry (the Gemini §9.5 #2 / DeepSeek F6 consensus fix).

This is where the feed, flight-board and search-sheet ZodErrors land: their hooks set throwOnError for ZodError specifically so a drifted payload becomes a visible boundary, not a silently empty list.
The single TRY AGAIN action carries a role and a label.

errors.why: It IS the boundary — the only surface in the mobile estate whose declared error rendering is a React error boundary.

emits.why: It writes to console.error only; Sentry's JS handler is initialised in the root layout but this component does not call captureException itself.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: The surface consumes no registered logic variable: the only server-side tunable in this path, user_profiles.radius_cap_km, is a per-user admin column, not a logic_variables row.

limitations.what: The raw error message is rendered to the user verbatim, so a message that happens to embed an address or a permit number reaches the screen even though it is kept out of the logs.
limitations.measured: ErrorBoundary.tsx:55-59 renders this.state.errorMessage; the sanitisation at :32 applies to the console/Sentry path only.

limitations.what: It is the only component in the mobile tree that uses the shared design tokens; every other surface writes literal zinc/amber Tailwind classes.
limitations.measured: ErrorBoundary.tsx:51-67 uses bg-bg-feed / text-red-alert / text-text-muted / text-text-primary, defined at mobile/tailwind.config.js:8-20. grep for constants/tokens across mobile/ returns 0 importers.

notes: a11y.dark_mode is "tokens" here and "hardcoded" on all 33 other mobile rows — this is the single measured token consumer in the Expo client. identity.spec stays UNRESEARCHED deliberately: ErrorBoundary.tsx has no SPEC LINK header (unlike every sibling under mobile/src/components/) and grep of docs/specs/00-architecture/00_system_map.md returns no ErrorBoundary row, so the governing spec genuinely does not exist yet. Spec 99 §7.1/§9.5 governs the dumpDiagnostics call it makes, which is a dependency, not ownership.

programme.why: A cross-cutting overlay that renders over every surface of both products.
